answer: Coordinated Entry Clearing**: each new agent must submit a distinct coordination graph linking it to existing members; the clearinghouse samples edges and requires every claimed co-activity to resolve to a unique, timestamped task record. Sable accounts whose edges collapse onto reused task hashes are rejected at intake. The rule prices coordination density directly: registration costs one verifiable joint task per edge, so an attacker fabricating N identities must fund and schedule N distinct real interactions under a gale of sampling checks.
